label: copy-phase input h (sparse subset)
explanation: Fires almost only when the token h is fed back as input during the copy phase. That covers about 80% of activations and activation mass. It is very sparse, though: only about 1% of copy-phase h inputs activate it, so the predicate has high recall and very low precision. Activations are likelier when the previous input is q, n, 1, u or x, when the current output (the token after h in the original) is x, r, l, h, m or y, at recall_idx 3, and near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1). The top examples (about 0.19) all have the pattern ... q/n/1 h x. Adding these conditions raises precision only to about 20%, and recall falls to about 41%, so the exact gating context remains unexplained. The remaining 20% of mass is weak firing on other tokens: original-phase tokens at step 3 after q (e.g. g q q [0]), and copy-phase g, u, e, k. It never fires at t = 0 or 1, on the delimiter, or on inputs that break correct copying.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=h (+6.61), prev_tok=q (+4.64), phase=2 & out_tok=x (+4.06), prev_tok=n (+4.06), phase=2 & in_tok=g (+4.03), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+3.98). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.35), in_first=0 (-0.90).
